nt: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. This marks the shift from the previous accusations to the sentence or judgement about to be pronounced. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [Because you do these things]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as a common expression to mean that he is about to act. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to devise]

Yahweh is using one part of the nation, **this clan** to represent all the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all of you]

Yahweh is speaking of the coming disaster as if it were a heavy yoke on the people, from which **you will not remove your necks**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will not conduct yourselves proudly]

nt: Micah is using the phrase translated as **In that day** to introduce a new event. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Micah is repeating forms of the word **lament** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. The people are repeating forms of the same verb, **Destroying** and **we are destroyed**, in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. Micah assumes that readers will know that **casting a measuring line by lot** refers to the way the tribes received the land in [Numbers 26:55](../../num/26/55.md). Since Yahweh had promised Abraham the land as an eternal inheritance, Micah knew they would some day return from exile and the land would once again be divided up, but those who Yahweh is judging here will not be a part of that. You could say that explicitly as in the UST if that would be helpful to your readers.

Micah is using the possessive form to mean the **assembly** that belongs to **Yahweh,** that is, when his people gather once again to divide up the land after returning from exile. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [among Yahweh’s people]
